Unclaimed estates list

A list of unclaimed estates held by the Treasury Solicitor. Last updated 28th August 2026.

From:
Bona Vacantia and Government Legal Department
Published:
6 December 2013
Last updated:
28 August 2026 — See all updates

Contents

  1. The list
  2. Disclaimer

The Bona Vacantia Division (BVD) publishes a list of unclaimed estates which have been referred to it but not yet claimed within the time limit for doing so.

The list

Unclaimed estates list (CSV, 341 KB)

The list is published in a Comma Separated Values (CSV) file format. This acts like a spreadsheet and although it can be opened in any text editor it is best viewed in a spreadsheet application, such as Microsoft Excel, Google Docs or OpenOffice Calc.

If you cannot find your relative on the BVD list, which is updated regularly, then it is likely that BVD is not dealing with their estate.  There are other sources of information which may assist:

  • You can obtain the death certificate and contact the person who registered the death General Register Office - GOV.UK (www.gov.uk)
  • You can contact the relevant Local Authority where the person died as they may have undertaken the funeral
  • You can obtain a copy of any Grant of Probate or Administration if one has been issued to contact the person dealing with the estate Search probate records for documents and wills (England and Wales) - GOV.UK
  • You can search for any estate notices which may have been placed in the Notices Wills and Probate The Gazette

If your relative is on the BVD list, then refer to the Make a claim to a deceased person’s estate section of this website

Disclaimer

The list cannot be guaranteed to be complete and correct and no warranties are given or implied to that effect. Copies of the list held on other sources or provided by third parties other than BVD cannot be guaranteed to be accurate or up to date. BVD does not accept any responsibility for any loss whatsoever which might result from reliance thereon.

Please note that the list may be removed, amended or modified (including, but not limited to, its content, structure and/or format) at any time without notice.
